newsitem.title: USA: Wyser-Pratte seeks voting trust for Conrail.
newsitem.headline: Wyser-Pratte seeks voting trust for Conrail.

text.p: Wyser-Pratte & Co Inc said it will propose that Norfolk Southern Corp sponsor a voting trust to control issues regarding the repeal of Conrail Inc's antitakeover provisions.
The trust would seek to control at least 50 percent of the vote of Conrail's shareholders, said company president Guy Wyser-Pratte.

Conrail has rejected a $10.3 billion takeover offer from Norfolk Southern in favor of a $9.4 billion merger with CSX Corp. But Conrail shareholders last week rejected a measure that was critical to the planned union with CSX.
"This mechanism may be the most effective means of breaking the current stalemate and ensuring that Conrail's board acts in the interests of its shareholders," Wyser-Pratte said in a news release.
Spokesmen for Norfolk Southern and Conrail were not immediately available for comment.

Wyser-Pratte said participating shareholders would cede to the voting trust for four years all rights to vote on issues regarding the repeal of Conrail's antitakeover provisions. Conrail shareholders would retain any economic benefits associated with the shares and also would keep the rights to sell their shares, tender their shares into a tender offer and vote on all matters other than Conrail's antitakeover provisions.
